name: agenthop
description: AgentHop is a diagnostic benchmark for multi-step scientific question answering: 1,011 four-option multiple-choice questions grounded in citation chains over 7,205 arXiv papers from nine major computer-science venues (2022-2025). Each question is answerable only by reading specific sections of one or two of these papers; the agent reaches the answer-bearing papers by following references from a given seed paper. The dataset is paired with a four-axis decomposition framework (search, synthesis, tool-use pattern, resource management) that turns a single evaluation run into per-model failure-mode attribution rather than a single accuracy number.

rai:dataCollection: AgentHop is built from public arXiv papers across nine major computer-science venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, CVPR, ECCV, SIGIR), publication years 2022-2025. Paper metadata is fetched via the arXiv API; full body content is parsed from ar5iv (the arXiv HTML rendering service), with arXiv-hosted HTML fallback. Items are constructed via an eight-stage pipeline: seed selection, citation-chain expansion, corpus collection, question/answer generation, distractor generation, model-ensemble filtering, seven-auditor human review, and post-audit triage.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public arXiv papers under their respective arXiv-deposited licenses (predominantly arXiv-perpetual and CC-BY family). Only paper identifiers, abstracts, and named-section text are used; figures, tables, and non-textual content are not redistributed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-5.4 generates question/answer pairs (Stage 3) and audit-prep items (Stage 5). A three-model ensemble (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.6, deepseek-chat) performs shortcut-detection and consensus filtering (Stages 6-7). Seven human auditors (two MS, five PhD candidates in computer science) review audit-prep items via a structured Gradio interface, recording one of three verdicts (Pass / Flag / Remove) plus free-text notes on flagged items. The lead author then triages all flagged items in a follow-up pass. Verbatim system prompts for every LLM-driven stage are released in the paper's Appendix.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom Gradio web interface for human review.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Construction-time consensus tiers (Gold / Silver / Bronze) record filter agreement among the three-model ensemble. Auditor verdicts are released as derived consensus tiers and section-recall labels in audit/recall_labels.jsonl. Post-audit triage retired 35 of 116 flagged samples; full triage-decision themes are documented in the paper's Appendix B.
rai:dataAnnotationDemographics: All seven auditors are members of the research team and participated voluntarily as part of the paper's data-curation process. No external paid annotation was used. No personal information of auditors is collected or released.
rai:dataIntendedUseStatement: Diagnostic evaluation of multi-step scientific question-answering agents along four axes: navigation, synthesis, tool-use pattern, and resource management. Aggregate accuracy is intended to be paired with the per-axis decomposition; AgentHop scores should not be used in isolation as the basis for model-selection decisions, nor interpreted as evidence of capability differences in unrelated tasks.
rai:dataUseCases: Per-axis failure-mode attribution for multi-paper QA agents
Comparison of agentic loop competence across model families and capability tiers
Within-family generation-gap analysis on agentic tasks
rai:dataLimitations: Single domain: computer-science papers from nine major venues (2022-2025).
Multiple-choice format only; not a free-form generation task.
Generator-evaluator overlap: GPT-5.4 generated the items and is also among the evaluated models. Effect is bounded but real and acknowledged in the paper's Limitations section.
Parametric coverage: the strongest checkpoints already resolve a substantial fraction of items closed-book; the four-axis decomposition is most informative where parametric coverage is sparse.

Citation-graph coverage: roughly 57 percent of papers in the per-query two-hop neighbourhood are metadata-only (no parsed body), reflecting realistic arXiv coverage gaps. The seed-to-bridge-to-target chain of every sample is guaranteed to have full content.
rai:dataBiases: Source venues are computer-science conferences with high arXiv-deposit rates; venues with lower deposit rates and non-arXiv conference proceedings are not represented. The benchmark therefore reflects the topical and authorial composition of arXiv computer-science deposits over 2022-2025.
rai:dataSocialImpact: AgentHop is a diagnostic measurement instrument; it does not produce content or model weights. Positive impact: per-axis attribution helps developers and users understand where multi-paper QA agents fail (retrieval vs. synthesis vs. tool-use vs. resource management) more precisely than aggregate accuracy. Potential negative impact: leaderboard rankings may be misinterpreted as generic model-quality signals; we explicitly recommend pairing AgentHop scores with established benchmarks for the deployment-relevant target task.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The released asset contains no personal information about study participants, no harmful or offensive content, and no generative model weights. Source content is publicly-available scholarly papers; auditor identifying information is not collected or released.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Released on Hugging Face under CC-BY 4.0 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/agenthop/agenthop). Maintained by anonymous authors during peer review and by the named authors after camera-ready. The benchmark items, citation graphs, paper-pool section text, and auditor section-recall labels are fixed; any post-release corrections will be issued as versioned updates with a documented changelog.
